"# A Preventable Tragedy in Darwin

The palm tree on the corner of Stuart Highway and Bargot Road bears the scars of September 16th—a day that would end in heartbreak and institutional failure. When two Northern Territory police officers arrived at the scene of the crash, they found Dale Scott Walkinshaw, 23, cradling his passenger behind some vegetation. The young woman had suffered a serious back injury and drifted in and out of consciousness. Walkinshaw's blood alcohol level told the story: 0.149, nearly three times the legal limit.

What happened next—Walkinshaw's arrest and placement in a caged police van—would become the final chapter in a tragedy that years of negligence had made almost inevitable.

The coroner's findings paint a damning picture of institutional indifference. NT coroner Greg Cavanagh didn't mince words: between a previous death in custody in 2013 and Walkinshaw's death last year, there were at least 16 attempted suicides in caged police vehicles. In six cases, officers didn't discover the desperate individuals until they were semi-conscious or unconscious.

An internal report had recommended installing CCTV cameras in 2013—a simple, practical measure that might have prevented tragedy. But the recommendation languished, ignored by a system that seemed determined to ignore warning signs.

"It wasn't a matter of if a person would die in the back of a police van but when," Cavanagh concluded grimly.

The coroner's words echo with the weight of preventable loss."
